bug_description.original: Heap-use-after-free in r_list_free OSS-Fuzz report: https://bugs.chromium.org/p/oss-fuzz/issues/detail?id=390467754 ``` Crash type: Heap-use-after-free READ 8 Crash state: r_list_free r_bin_bflt_free r_bin_file_free ```
bug_description.normalized: In the radare2 bFLT bin plugin, relocs() allocates an RList for relocation records and stores the original list pointer in obj->relocs_list before returning it. r_bin_object_set_items then calls the plugin relocs callback, converts the returned list into bo->relocs, and frees that returned RList wrapper. For the 8-byte PoC, the parsed bFLT header has revision 4 and all remaining fields zero, so relocs() returns an empty list; freeing the wrapper still leaves obj->relocs_list dangling. Later, plugin destroy calls r_bin_bflt_free, which calls r_list_free(o->relocs_list) on the freed list header, causing a heap-use-after-free READ of size 8 inside r_list_free/r_list_purge.

source.description: First project-code read of attacker-controlled input. The bFLT loader copies bytes from the fuzzed file buffer into the local header array bhdr, from which revision and relocation-related header fields are parsed.
source.value_from: The libFuzzer harness writes the attacker-controlled Data/Size buffer into a malloc-backed file via r_io_write_at, then the bFLT plugin reads that file buffer through RBuffer when loading the binary.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant state originates from the short 8-byte PoC being read into the zero-initialized bhdr array. Only the magic and revision bytes are supplied by the file; the remaining header fields stay zero because bhdr was initialized with {0}, leading to flags=0 and reloc_count=0 in the parsed header.

root_cause.description: relocs() stores the original RList wrapper in obj->relocs_list before returning that same list to the caller. r_bin_object_set_items later assumes ownership of the returned list wrapper and frees it, but obj->relocs_list is not cleared or replaced. The fix removes this early assignment, stores obj->relocs_list only after successful construction, and returns a clone so plugin state no longer aliases the caller-freed wrapper.

sink.description: Dereferences the already-freed RList header through the stale obj->relocs_list pointer. r_list_purge reads list metadata (such as head, tail, length, and free callback) from the freed list wrapper, producing the observed AddressSanitizer heap-use-after-free READ of size 8.

parser_admitted.description: The short file is admitted as bFLT because the earlier magic check at line 25 matches "bFLT" and the parsed revision equals FLAT_VERSION (4), so the rejection branch is not taken.

fine_trace.note: Copies the attacker-controlled file bytes into the local bhdr array. bhdr was initialized with {0}, so with the 8-byte PoC only bhdr[0..7] come from input and the remaining header bytes stay zero.
reachability_checkpoints: Harness wrote exactly 8 bytes to the malloc-backed file before binary loading

fine_trace.note: Materializes header fields from bhdr. For this PoC, p_hdr->rev becomes 4 from bytes 4..7, while later parsed fields including p_hdr->reloc_count and p_hdr->flags become 0 because the unread portion of bhdr remained zeroed.
The revision check passes because p_hdr->rev == 4, so execution continues to bin->hdr = p_hdr at line 52. This admits the crafted file into the bFLT loader with reloc_count=0 and flags=0.

Allocates the relocation-list wrapper that will later become dangling. Because the PoC yields no GOT and no reloc entries, this wrapper stays empty; the bug is on the wrapper lifetime itself, not on any relocation element stored inside it.
Caches the original list wrapper in plugin state before ownership is settled. obj->relocs_list and the local list variable now alias the same RList object.

Both population branches are skipped: obj->hdr->flags does not contain FLAT_FLAG_GOTPIC at line 132 and obj->hdr->reloc_count is 0 here, so no relocation entries are appended. relocs() reaches line 230 and returns the same empty list wrapper from steps 3-4.
Hands the original RList wrapper back to the caller without cloning it. The returned pointer is still the same object cached in obj->relocs_list.

depends_on.via: relocs() exits through the success return

fine_trace.note: Object setup enters the relocation-loading path and calls the plugin's relocs callback. This control decision is required for the caller to receive and later free the list wrapper returned by relocs().
Receives the exact same RList pointer created in relocs(). The caller-local l aliases obj->relocs_list because relocs() returned the original wrapper instead of a clone.

After converting the returned list to bo->relocs and nulling l->free, the caller frees the RList wrapper itself. obj->relocs_list was not cleared, so plugin state now holds a dangling pointer to the freed list header.
Teardown reloads the stale list pointer from plugin state and passes it back to r_list_free a second time during destroy -> r_bin_bflt_free.

Sink. r_list_free dereferences the freed RList header by calling r_list_purge(list), which reads list fields from the already-freed wrapper. ASan reports heap-use-after-free READ of size 8 with crash state r_list_free -> r_bin_bflt_free -> r_bin_file_free.

allocation_context.description: The freed object is the RList wrapper allocated by r_list_newf((RListFree) free) in relocs().

free_context.description: The caller frees the returned list wrapper with r_list_free(l) after converting it to bo->relocs, leaving obj->relocs_list dangling.

sanitizer_ground_truth.source: reproduction_report.json, sanitizer_trace.txt, default_crash_trace.txt, patch.diff, and vulnerable-source inspection

cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The fix removes the early obj->relocs_list assignment, assigns plugin state only after successful list construction, and returns r_list_clone(list, NULL) instead of the original wrapper, so the caller can free its copy without leaving obj->relocs_list dangling.

format.name: Raw bFLT header prefix consumed by radare2's bFLT loader
format.contract: Exactly the witnessed 8-byte blob `62 46 4c 54 00 00 00 04` (`"bFLT"` followed by big-endian revision 4). Because bflt_init_hdr initializes its 64-byte local header buffer to zero before reading, this short input leaves the rest of the header fields at zero, so the file is admitted as bFLT with `flags == 0` and `reloc_count == 0`. That singular combination is sufficient for relocs() to cache an empty `RList` in `obj->relocs_list`, return the same wrapper to `r_bin_object_set_items`, and later trigger the stale-wrapper free path during teardown.
